terms.definition: The average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km, used as a measuring stick for distances inside the solar system.
terms.function: Lets astronomers compare planet distances with small numbers — Mercury at 0.4 AU, Neptune at 30 AU — instead of millions of kilometres.
terms.whereItIs: Shown as the floating scale bar above the planet line in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the standard 'ruler' of the solar system; every orbit in this branch is measured against it.

terms.definition: A model where sizes and distances are reduced by the same factor, so the proportions stay true.
terms.function: Reveals the real proportions of the solar system that ordinary diagrams hide.
terms.whereItIs: The true-distance mode of the model is a scale model; the size-only mode is not.
terms.whyItMatters: Only a true scale model shows how tiny the planets are and how vast the gaps between them are.

terms.definition: How long light takes to cross a given distance; light covers about 300,000 km every second.
terms.function: Turns huge distances into times you can compare — 8 minutes to Earth, hours to the outer planets.
terms.whereItIs: Displayed on the AU scale bar readout in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is a way to 'feel' distances: the Sun's light you see now left it 8 minutes ago.

terms.definition: The four planets nearest the Sun — Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars — all small, rocky worlds.
terms.function: Together they occupy the inner region of the solar system, within about 1.5 AU of the Sun.
terms.whereItIs: The compact cluster of small spheres between the Sun and the great gap in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the rocky planets — including our own — and they all fit inside the gap before Jupiter.

terms.definition: The four planets beyond the asteroid belt — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — giant, mostly gaseous worlds.
terms.function: Their sheer size dominates any planet lineup, yet in true-distance mode they recede into the far distance.
terms.whereItIs: The distant group of large spheres at the far end of the planet line.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the giants of the solar system, and their distance from the Sun drives the enormous gap in the model.
